title: Sparsity after a half-shift
statement: For every nonnegative integer $n$ and every real-valued function $q$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, the number of nonzero Fourier coefficients of the function $x\mapsto \tfrac12-q(x)$ is at most one more than the number of nonzero Fourier coefficients of $q$.
hypotheses_covered: $q$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
